questions.q: Which chapter in this course covered designing security for a real org, testing it, troubleshooting it, and a full audit case study?
options: Chapter 3 — Applying Security
Chapter 1 — The Security Model
Chapter 2 — Record Access
Chapter 4 — Beyond the Basics
questions.explain: Chapter 3, 'Applying Security,' covered the sales/service org designs, restriction and scoping rules, Login As/Run As testing, troubleshooting, common mistakes, and the audit case study.

questions.q: How does this course's scope compare to the Sharing and Visibility Architect specialization mentioned in this lesson?
options: They cover exactly the same material at the same depth
The Architect specialization replaces the need for this course entirely
This course covers correct use of the full toolbox for a typical org; the Architect specialization goes deeper into scale, performance, and defensible design tradeoffs
This course is more advanced than the Architect specialization
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this course is fundamentals-level, while the Architect path goes further into scale (millions of records/users), recalculation performance tuning, and deep territory design.

questions.q: What hands-on practice does this lesson recommend before moving on to the next course?
options: Only re-reading the guide.md files for each lesson
Memorizing every quiz question verbatim
Waiting for a live instructor-led session before practicing anything
Building Lesson 14's design from scratch in a free org, verifying it with Login As, then deliberately breaking and troubleshooting it
questions.explain: The lesson's practice recommendation is hands-on: rebuild the Meridian Outfitters design, verify with Login As, and practice the Lesson 18 troubleshooting order on a deliberately introduced problem.

questions.q: What is the next course in the Salesforce Administrator path after Security & Access Fundamentals?
options: Salesforce Admin Reports and Dashboards
Salesforce Data Management
Apex Programming
Salesforce Integration Development
questions.explain: The lesson names Salesforce Data Management as the next course, covering how data gets into, is cleaned within, and is maintained in the org.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a learner be able to do if they're ready to move on to Salesforce Data Management?
options: List the four chapter titles in order and describe one thing each one covered, from memory
Recite every quiz answer from the course by number
Pass a Salesforce certification exam
Rebuild the entire course's slide deck
questions.explain: The lesson's 'check yourself' explicitly frames readiness as being able to recall the four chapters and what each covered, without looking back at the material.
